key_insight: A DistilGPT2 table-to-text approach can turn small, imbalanced clinical datasets into strong disease prediction models by leveraging contextual language patterns rather than relying only on traditional feature statistics.
clinical_relevance: This could help improve early disease risk prediction in low-volume clinical settings where conventional machine learning models often miss minority-case patterns.
method: Converted structured patient records into physician-style text descriptions
Augmented minority-class examples with GPT-4-generated medical paraphrases
Fine-tuned DistilGPT2 and used gradient-based explainability to highlight important clinical features
evidence_signal: Across four public datasets, the model reported average precision, specificity, sensitivity, and F1-score of 0.96, 0.97, 0.96, and 0.96, respectively, with stronger sensitivity and stability than several comparison methods.
watch_item: Results come from public datasets, so real-world performance and safety need external validation before clinical deployment.
paper_title: Can GPT Be Used as an Alternative Prediction Model to Traditional Machine Learning and Neural Networks on Low-Volume Clinical Data?
